purpose: Research-only handoff for nums 595-606, 618, 619, and 914-919. Built from live Common Sense Media refetches of catalog srcUrl pages where available plus targeted lookup for non-CSM or missing catalog URLs. Do not treat as production data until reviewed and transformed through the official workflow.

contentFlagModel.mappingNote: This refetch preserves CSM's current visible category label and proposes the nearest app level. Production catalog edits should be made only by the follow-up importer/reviewer.

entries.title: Now and Then

violence.summary: CSM notes Jell-O thrown at girls, newspaper descriptions of a burglary, murder, and fatal crash, a bloody-nose punch, a fake drowning panic, and a storm-drain flood rescue.

language.summary: Language includes moderate profanity, crude body terms, sexual slang, insults, and bathroom words.

romance.summary: Preteen body anxiety, breast-size jokes, misleading sex talk corrected by friends, boys skinny-dipping, comments about penis size, hard-on references, and visible boys' backsides drive the category.

drinking.summary: Kids try cigarettes, adults smoke, and a man says drinking in a bar may have kept him from protecting his family.

handoffNotes: Sexual-development and body-image details are central to CSM's age rating.

entries.title: The Mighty Ducks

violence.summary: Hockey body-checking, shoving, light wrestling, one player knocked unconscious without lasting injury, an alley scuffle, and a groin-impact gag are the main violence notes.

language.summary: Adults and kids use mild-to-moderate profanity, sexist sports insults, and a couple of double entendres.

romance.summary: Kids excitedly look through swimsuit magazines, an adult brags about a sexual conquest, adults date and kiss, and there are mild double entendres.

drinking.summary: An early scene has a character drink and drive, then get pulled over and arrested for DUI.

handoffNotes: DUI is the key substance-content signal.

entries.title: Beethoven

violence.summary: An illegal stolen-dog testing scheme, threats involving exploding bullets, bullying, dog and human fights, fake blood, syringe injuries, near-drowning, a child car crash, Wolfman footage, and a suicide phrase create moderate peril.

language.summary: Mild profanity, insults, a child-written innuendo, a "dog killer" accusation, and a casual "I'll kill myself" line are noted.

romance.summary: A husband mistakes the dog for his wife in bed and makes sexual comments while being licked, plus there is romantic kissing and a dog-name innuendo.

drinking.summary: An adult briefly smokes, and the villain plot implies drug testing on dogs with syringes and medical restraints.

handoffNotes: Animal testing and dog peril are the main sensitive-viewer issues.

entries.title: 3 Ninjas

violence.summary: Frequent choreographed fights put kids against adults, with swords, nunchaku, guns, minor bloody injuries, a thrown knife, a gunshot wound, kidnapping, armed robbery, bullying, tied-up adults, and violent song lyrics.

language.summary: Language includes mild insults, ableist slurs, religious exclamations, rude bumper-sticker wording, and repeated poop and toilet terms.

romance.summary: Sexual innuendo includes men looking at a racy magazine, repeated groin hits, bathroom-pants gags, boxers shown after a sword slices pants, and diarrhea-prank exposure humor.

drinking.summary: One person is about to light a cigarette before a fight.

handoffNotes: This is the slice's clearest level 4 violence title.

entries.title: Jumanji

violence.summary: Sustained peril includes wildlife attacks, a bullied boy with injuries, a maniacal hunter firing at characters, children dangling over raging water, and frightening game-suction effects.

language.summary: CSM notes a couple uses of "damn."

romance.summary: CSM does not surface sex, romance, or nudity content.

drinking.summary: CSM does not surface drinking, drug, or smoking content.

handoffNotes: Animal peril and body-disintegration effects are likely the most relevant scariness details.

entries.title: Mrs. Doubtfire

violence.summary: CSM notes brief bullying and arguments.

language.summary: Language includes one strong profanity instance, other moderate profanity, sexual-size jokes, and a middle-finger gesture.

romance.summary: Sexual content includes questions about a mother's sex life and partners, Daniel bare-chested while changing, and dinner-table innuendo.

drinking.summary: Adults drink alcohol, an animated bird smokes in the opening, and adults smoke indoors in a scene the main character criticizes.

handoffNotes: Strong language is the main reason this skews older than most titles in the slice.

entries.title: The Addams Family

violence.summary: Macabre violence includes weapons, a biting bear rug, choking, falls, torture-machine stretching, children using arrows and an electric chair, fake-blood performance, presumed villain deaths, fiery train crash, burial and rotting-body talk, molestation mention, and a fairy-tale burning discussion.

language.summary: Language includes mild profanity, religious exclamations, and insults such as "moron," "deadbeat," "parasite," and "demented freak."

romance.summary: Strong married-couple innuendo includes many kisses, pleasure tied to torture devices, Morticia enjoying being tied up, public making out, orgasmic sounds, and a cleavage-kiss cuckoo clock gag.

drinking.summary: A character smokes cigars and says he started at age five, and adults drink spirits.

handoffNotes: Macabre child-play violence and sexualized married-couple humor both need explicit review.

entries.title: Hook

violence.summary: Pirate peril includes kidnapped children, net traps, gunfire, sword fights, dead bodies, a boy killed by Hook's blade, bloody hook injury, shootings, knife chases, torture with scorpions, crocodile death, falls, crotch gags, a suicide threat, nonconsensual sleeping kiss, airplane fear, and a crying lost baby.

language.summary: Language includes mild profanity, "fornicate," many insults about age and size, a long name-calling exchange, and a father yelling harshly at his kids.

romance.summary: Sexual content includes a brothel and sex workers, suggestive hook removal, mermaid kisses, other kisses including a nonconsensual one, comments on legs and beauty, crotch-sniffing flowers, and a pants-slashing gag.

drinking.summary: Adults drink wine and whiskey, a Neverland bar is named The Drunken Wench, one character is told they drink too much, Hook smokes two cigars at once, and drugs are referenced.

handoffNotes: Contains several nuance notes: suicide threat, child death, brothel imagery, and nonconsensual kiss.

entries.title: Heavyweights

violence.summary: Tony is tied up and placed in an electric-fence cage, and a father punches him in the stomach near the end.

language.summary: Language includes a few mild-to-moderate phrases such as "damn," "big ass," "see you in hell," and "kick his ass."

romance.summary: CSM labels romance as none while noting teens making out in the credits and at a dance, plus a counselor kissing the camp nurse.

drinking.summary: Food addiction is framed with drug-like language and behavior, and adults including the cameraman and cook smoke cigarettes.

handoffNotes: Food-as-drug framing is the main CSM substance signal.

entries.title: Mouse Hunt

violence.summary: Frequent pratfall violence includes a bloodied exterminator being dragged, Three Stooges-style head-bashing with household objects, broad cartoon mayhem, and one brother pointing a loaded shotgun at the other's face.

language.summary: Language includes moderate profanity and sexual innuendo involving nature-film sex talk, a cat-related double entendre, and a mouse-in-pants gag while a fly is unzipped.

romance.summary: Sexualized slapstick includes a man nearly naked with string covering his private parts, his wife on a desk in lingerie, a mouse falling into cleavage, and men reaching down women's dresses to catch or imitate catching the mouse.

drinking.summary: Characters drink alcohol at a reception.

handoffNotes: Loaded-shotgun gag and sexualized slapstick are the main handoff items.

entries.title: The Little Rascals

violence.summary: Bullies threaten Alfalfa and Spanky, a large dog scares Alfalfa, a dream fall lands him on rocks, go-carts knock people over, Alfalfa punches Woim, and the clubhouse catches fire.

language.summary: CSM flags child-level double entendres involving a lizard, pickle, "boy toy," "number two," and "fairy," plus bully phrases such as "bite me" and "losers suck."

romance.summary: Children kiss several times, Alfalfa appears in underwear and is implied to be naked off-screen, A.J. kisses Spanky on the cheeks, and a girl uses the phrase "boy toy."

drinking.summary: During a pretend fancy date, Alfalfa and Darla drink grape juice from pudding glasses and make wine-related references.

handoffNotes: Several innuendo jokes are delivered by children, which may need careful tone in production copy.

entries.title: The Parent Trap

violence.summary: Mild content includes an ear-piercing scream, a woman falling into a lake and reacting to a lizard, and mean-spirited camp pranks and teasing.

language.summary: Language includes "two-faced little brat" and "God" as an exclamation.

romance.summary: Adults kiss and embrace warmly, a girl must jump naked into a lake after losing a bet with no actual nudity shown, and a man walks around in a Speedo.

drinking.summary: A main character owns a vineyard, wine drinking appears in many scenes, an 11-year-old tastes wine at dinner, and one character anxiously smokes and drinks too much.

handoffNotes: Wine and underage tasting are stronger signals than the otherwise gentle tone.

entries.title: Anne of Green Gables

violence.summary: Anne sometimes lashes out or lands in mild peril, including walking on a roof and floating in a leaky boat; a key death is very sad, a baby's illness is tense, and school discipline is stricter than today.

language.summary: CSM does not surface language content.

romance.summary: There is very mild flirting and romance, plus a teacher giving eyebrow-raising special attention to a teen student by modern standards.

drinking.summary: Anne accidentally gets Diana drunk at a tea party because of a bottle mix-up.

handoffNotes: Emotional intensity from death and illness may matter more than category levels suggest.

entries.title: The Adventures of Milo and Otis

violence.summary: Real animals face more danger than expected for a G-rated movie, including encounters with bears, hedgehogs, seagulls, crayfish, a cliff jump, a night alone in the dark, and close calls with predatory bears.

language.summary: Mild threatening phrases include "you're dead meat," "make my doggie day," and "cruddy."

romance.summary: Milo and Otis each meet mates, the couples romp together, and kitten and puppy births are shown.

drinking.summary: CSM does not surface drinking, drug, or smoking content.

handoffNotes: CSM's review also references long-standing animal-rights concerns around how the film was made, outside the four requested flags.

entries.title: Popeye

violence.summary: CSM surfaces cartoonish fights between Popeye and villains, including Bluto.

language.summary: CSM notes a few instances of very mild cursing.

romance.summary: CSM does not surface sex, romance, or nudity content.

drinking.summary: CSM does not surface drinking, drug, or smoking content.

handoffNotes: CSM detail text is sparse; confidence is still high because the live category metadata is present.

entries.title: All Dogs Go to Heaven

violence.summary: Cartoon violence and demonic imagery include character deaths, Anne-Marie threatened with death in a river of fire and nearly drowning, repeated kidnapping, gambling exploitation, theft, arson, gunfire during an escape, and a villain trying to kill the protagonist with a car and water.

language.summary: CSM does not surface language content.

romance.summary: CSM does not surface sex, romance, or nudity content.

drinking.summary: Dogs drink at a bar, fall over and pass out, sing while drunk, one dog smokes and blows cigar smoke in Anne-Marie's face, and a horse smokes a cigarette.

handoffNotes: Substance content is level 4, and death/river-of-fire peril should be noted clearly.

entries.title: Mickey's Christmas Carol

violence.summary: Scary moments include the Ghost of Christmas Future and a burning coffin, plus comic Pluto's Christmas Tree violence where Mickey wrings Pluto's neck and insults him.

language.summary: CSM does not surface a current language rating or visible language detail.

romance.summary: Daisy Duck flirtatiously wants a kiss from Scrooge, kisses his cheek, and his eyes and heart react wildly.

drinking.summary: Cigar and cigarette smoking appear in the Christmas Carol cartoon.

entries.title: My Little Pony: The Movie

violence.summary: Cartoon action includes evil witches casting spells, smooze flooding Ponyland, Hydia abusing her daughters, ponies threatened by monster-spiders, underground growls, menacing trees, slime-spewing creatures, chases, falls, cliff danger, and narrow escapes.

language.summary: The witches insult each other with mild phrases such as "shut up," "stupid," "pea brain," and "do-nothings."

romance.summary: CSM does not surface sex, romance, or nudity content.

drinking.summary: CSM does not surface drinking, drug, or smoking content.

handoffNotes: Fantasy menace is broad but cartoonish and aimed at young viewers.

entries.title: The Wiz

violence.summary: Frightening fantasy imagery includes living graffiti, subway marionettes, attacking trash cans, crow harassment, flying monkeys, a fire-breathing head, a visible dead body, electrocution, drugged unconsciousness, an interrupted suicide attempt, enslaved factory workers, torture, threats to burn a dog, and an off-screen melting death.

language.summary: Language includes "hell" and frequent colorful put-downs such as "stupid," "garbage guts," "hulking she-devil," "mangy mutt," and similar insults.

romance.summary: Characters kiss passionately, poison poppies are women in tight clothing who lure characters with suggestive dancing, released factory workers dance in underwear, and a man asks if he can take Dorothy home.

drinking.summary: Adults drink and smoke at Thanksgiving, a song mentions wine, and poison poppies use dust that drugs characters unconscious.

handoffNotes: Interrupted suicide attempt, enslaved factory workers, torture imagery, and drugging should be retained in prose.
